deviations: Post-double-selection lasso implemented by hand (glmnet/hdm/lassopack unavailable): rigorous plug-in lasso following lassopack rlasso defaults as I understand them -- cluster-robust penalty loadings by clinic (psi_j = sqrt((1/N) sum_g (sum_{i in g} x_ij e_i)^2)), lambda = 2*1.1*sqrt(N)*qnorm(1 - gamma/(2p)) with gamma = 0.1/log(number of clusters), initial residuals from OLS on the 5 most correlated regressors, 2 loading iterations using post-lasso residuals. The authors' exact lasso implementation (pdslasso vs Stata dsregress, heteroskedastic vs cluster loadings, gamma) is not stated in the paper, so selected controls may differ.

Candidate controls taken as the analysis file's prebuilt CC* variables (23 individual controls with missing values mean-recoded plus missing dummies, and their 249 pairwise interactions) and CL* clinic dummies (59); date dummies (DD*, plus constant) partialled out of all variables before the lassos and always included; final OLS with date fixed effects (date_morning_survey) and clinic-clustered SEs via fixest.

Treatment dummies are patient_voucher and doctor_voucher (scheduled assignment) as in the analysis file; PI (information) cross-cut not controlled, pooled across arms as the paper's equation (1) describes.
notes: Sample: rows with patient==1 (in-clinic survey patients, N=2753) for column 1 (outcome used_vouchers_admin, voucher redemption from admin records); columns 2-5 use the 2429 patients with prescription/purchase outcomes recorded (RXtreat_sev_simple_mal, treat_sev_simple_mal, RXtreat_severe_mal, treat_severe_mal). For each outcome, rlasso of y, patient_voucher and doctor_voucher on candidates; union of selections enters the final regression. Two exploratory runs (variable listing, sample/coding checks) printed no RESULT lines. The printed 'p(bP=bD)' diagnostic in stdout is actually fixest's joint Wald p-value for bP=bD=0 (mislabelled, not a scored quantity); the separate 't-test bP=bD' line is the equality test. No run hung.
